review.summary: Mercedes lead the championship with 630 points after 19 rounds, having taken 12 wins and 24 podiums. Antonelli tops their drivers on first in the standings with 380 points, clear of Russell who is fourth on 250. In Mexico City they added 23: Antonelli finished third from grid four for 15 points, Russell sixth after starting second.
review.lastRace: At the Mexico City Grand Prix, Antonelli completed the race in third from grid four for 15 points, while Russell finished sixth after starting on the second row to take 8 points. Both drivers finished.

review.summary: Ferrari sit second with 504 points after 19 rounds and two wins, behind Mercedes. Hamilton lead their pair on third in the standings with 259 against Leclerc's fifth place and 245. In Mexico City they scored 30: Hamilton took second from pole for 18, Leclerc fourth from grid three for 12.
review.lastRace: Hamilton finished second at the Mexico City Grand Prix after starting on pole for 18 points, the closest car behind the winner. Leclerc completed the race in fourth from grid three for 12 points.

review.summary: Red Bull are third with 382 points after 19 rounds and three wins. Verstappen head their lineup on second in the standings with 261, well ahead of Hadjar on eighth with 107 and Lawson on ninth with 83. In Mexico City Verstappen won from grid five; Hadjar finished ninth for two points.
review.lastRace: Verstappen took victory at the Mexico City Grand Prix, climbing from grid five to win and claim 25 points. Hadjar completed the race in ninth from grid seven for two points.

review.summary: McLaren are fourth with 365 points after 19 rounds and two wins. Norris lead their drivers on sixth with 221 against Piastri's seventh place and 144. In Mexico City they scored 10: Norris finished fifth from grid six, while Piastri completed the race thirteenth without points.
review.lastRace: Norris finished fifth at the Mexico City Grand Prix from grid six for 10 points. Piastri completed the race in thirteenth after starting on the twelfth grid slot but took no points.

review.summary: RB F1 Team are fifth with 108 points after 19 rounds without a win or podium. Lindblad lead their pair on eleventh with 38 against Tsunoda's twentieth place and one point. In Mexico City Lawson finished seventh from grid twenty-two for six points; Lindblad retired.
review.lastRace: Lawson finished seventh at the Mexico City Grand Prix, climbing from grid twenty-two to claim six points. Lindblad started on the eighth grid slot but retired without a finishing position and took no points.

review.summary: Alpine are sixth with 69 points after 19 rounds without a win or podium. Gasly lead their pair on tenth with 42 against Colapinto's twelfth place and 27. In Mexico City both finished but neither scored: Colapinto fifteenth from grid eleventh, Gasly seventeenth after starting ninth.
review.lastRace: At the Mexico City Grand Prix, Colapinto completed the race in fifteenth from grid eleventh without points. Gasly finished seventeenth having started on the ninth grid slot; neither Alpine car scored.

review.summary: Haas are seventh with 31 points after 19 rounds without a win or podium. Bearman lead their drivers on thirteenth with 23 against Ocon's sixteenth place and seven, with Hirakawa twenty-first on one point. In Mexico City Hirakawa scored from tenth.
review.lastRace: Hirakawa finished tenth at the Mexico City Grand Prix, climbing from grid eighteenth to take a point. Bearman started on the fourteenth grid slot but retired without a finishing position and took no points.

review.summary: Audi are eighth with 27 points after 19 rounds without a win or podium. Bortoleto lead their pair on fourteenth with 14 against Hülkenberg's fifteenth place and 13, a close contest. In Mexico City Bortoleto finished eighth for four points; Hülkenberg fourteenth from grid ten.
review.lastRace: Bortoleto completed the Mexico City Grand Prix in eighth from grid thirteenth to take four points. Hülkenberg finished fourteenth after starting on the tenth grid slot without points.

review.summary: Williams are ninth with 12 points after 19 rounds without a win or podium. Sainz lead their pair on eighteenth with 7 against Albon's nineteenth place and 5. In Mexico City both finished but neither scored: Albon eleventh from grid sixteenth, Sainz twelfth from grid fifteenth.
review.lastRace: At the Mexico City Grand Prix, Albon completed the race in eleventh from grid sixteenth without points. Sainz finished twelfth after starting on the fifteenth grid slot; neither Williams driver scored.

review.summary: Aston Martin are tenth with 7 points after 19 rounds without a win or podium. Alonso lead their pair on seventeenth with 7 against Stroll's twenty-second place and none. In Mexico City both retired: Stroll from grid nineteenth, Alonso from grid seventeenth.
review.lastRace: At the Mexico City Grand Prix both Aston Martin cars retired. Stroll started on the nineteenth grid slot without a finishing position; Alonso also retired having started on the seventeenth grid slot. Neither scored.

review.summary: Cadillac are eleventh with no points after 19 rounds and no wins or podiums. Their drivers sit at the bottom of the standings: Bottas twenty-third and Pérez twenty-fourth, both on zero. In Mexico City Pérez finished sixteenth from grid twentieth without points; Bottas retired from grid twenty-first.
review.lastRace: Pérez completed the Mexico City Grand Prix in sixteenth from grid twentieth without scoring. Bottas started on the twenty-first grid slot but retired without a finishing position; neither Cadillac driver took a point.

review.summary: Ducati top the teams' standings after 18 rounds, eight wins and fifteen podiums to their credit. Their riders fill the front of the championship: Marc Marquez leads on 399 points, well clear of Fabio Di Giannantonio on 265, with Alex Marquez on 197 and Francesco Bagnaia on 173. The remainder trail comfortably — Franco Morbidelli 65, Iker Lecuona 11 and Michele Pirro level on zero.
review.lastRace: Marc Marquez won the Grand Prix of Malaysia to take the full 25 points, with Alex Marquez third and Fabio Di Giannantonio eighth rounding out a strong haul. Franco Morbidelli tenth, Francesco Bagnaia thirteenth and Iker Lecuona fifteenth also scored.

review.summary: Aprilia sit second in the teams' standings after 18 rounds, eight wins and thirty-one podiums behind leaders Ducati. Jorge Martin is second on 355 points and Marco Bezzecchi third on 332, a close pair up front. Ai Ogura fifth on 278 and Raul Fernandez seventh on 236 follow, with Lorenzo Savadori well back on zero.
review.lastRace: Ai Ogura finished fourth to take 13 points and Marco Bezzecchi sixth for ten more at the Grand Prix of Malaysia, a solid round for Aprilia with both riders in the top six.

review.summary: KTM are third in the teams' standings after 18 rounds, two wins and eight podiums. Pedro Acosta lead their charge, fourth on 295 points, well clear of a second group: Enea Bastianini tenth on 134 and Brad Binder twelfth on 118. Maverick Viñales 22nd on 14, Pol Espargaro 25th on 5 and Jonas Folger level on zero round out the field.
review.lastRace: Pedro Acosta took second and 20 points at the Grand Prix of Malaysia, with Enea Bastianini fifth for 11 and Brad Binder ninth for seven. Maverick Viñales fourteenth scored a further two.

review.summary: Honda have had a difficult season, fourth after 18 rounds with no wins and no podiums. Luca Marini lead their riders on 117 points, ahead of Diogo Moreira on 78 and Johann Zarco on 51. Joan Mir sits eighteenth on 33, while Somkiat Chantra and Takaaki Nakagami are level on three, with Cal Crutchlow and Aleix Espargaro on zero.
review.lastRace: Luca Marini finished seventh to score nine points at the Grand Prix of Malaysia, Honda's only result of the round. Johann Zarco, Diogo Moreira and Joan Mir all failed to finish.

review.summary: Yamaha are fifth after 18 rounds with no wins and no podiums. Fabio Quartararo lead on 79 points, comfortably ahead of Jack Miller on 31 and Alex Rins on 29. Toprak Razgatlioglu sits 21st on 18 and Augusto Fernandez 24th on 6, the two trailing riders well clear of the rest.
review.lastRace: Fabio Quartararo eleventh and Alex Rins twelfth scored five and four points at the Grand Prix of Malaysia, Yamaha's only points of the round. Jack Miller sixteenth went points empty and Augusto Fernandez failed to finish.

review.summary: Jaguar TCS Racing lead the championship after seventeen rounds, on 288 points with four wins and ten podiums. Mitch Evans tops their drivers on 160, ahead of António Félix Da Costa's 128.
review.lastRace: At the London E-Prix, Evans finished fourth from fifth on the grid for 12 points, while Da Costa started ninth and finished fifteenth without scoring.

review.summary: Porsche are second after seventeen rounds on 271 points, with four wins and eight podiums. Pascal Wehrlein leads their drivers on 169, ahead of Nico Müller's 102.
review.lastRace: At the London E-Prix both Porsche cars failed to score: Nico Müller started fourth and finished twelfth, while Pascal Wehrlein dropped from third to fourteenth.

review.summary: Mahindra Racing are third on 252 points from seventeen rounds, with two wins and seven podiums. Edoardo Mortara leads their drivers on 137, ahead of Nyck De Vries's 115.
review.lastRace: Mahindra had a strong London E-Prix: Nyck De Vries took the front row and finished second for 21 points, with Edoardo Mortara third from second on the grid for 15.

review.summary: Andretti Formula E are fourth on 229 points from seventeen rounds, with two wins and seven podiums. Jake Dennis leads their drivers strongly on 164, well ahead of Felipe Drugovich's 65.
review.lastRace: A difficult London E-Prix for Andretti: Jake Dennis started sixteenth and finished eighteenth without scoring, while Felipe Drugovich dropped from eleventh to thirteenth also without points.

review.summary: Citroën Racing are fifth on 182 points from seventeen rounds, with one win and six podiums. Nick Cassidy leads their drivers on 114, ahead of Jean-Éric Vergne's 68.
review.lastRace: Citroën scored with both cars at the London E-Prix: Nick Cassidy finished sixth from seventh for 8 points, and Jean-Éric Vergne rose from twelfth to seventh for 6.

review.summary: Nissan Formula E Team are sixth on 157 points from seventeen rounds, with one win and six podiums. Oliver Rowland leads their drivers on 137, well ahead of Norman Nato's 20.
review.lastRace: Nissan picked up a few points at the London E-Prix: Oliver Rowland climbed from seventeenth to ninth for 3, and Norman Nato rose from nineteenth to tenth for 1.

review.summary: Envision Racing are seventh on 152 points from seventeen rounds, with no wins and two podiums. Sébastien Buemi leads their drivers on 97, ahead of Joel Eriksson's 55.
review.lastRace: At the London E-Prix, Sébastien Buemi climbed from tenth to fifth for 10 points, while Joel Eriksson started fifteenth and did not finish without scoring.

review.summary: Cupra Kiro are eighth on 128 points from seventeen rounds, with one win and three podiums. Josep Maria Martí leads their drivers slightly on 66, just ahead of Dan Ticktum's 62.
review.lastRace: At the London E-Prix, Josep Maria Martí finished eighth from thirteenth for 4 points, while Dan Ticktum dropped from eighth to sixteenth without scoring.

review.summary: DS Penske are ninth on 91 points from seventeen rounds, with one win and a single podium. Taylor Barnard leads their drivers on 68, ahead of Maximilian Günther's 23.
review.lastRace: Taylor Barnard won the London E-Prix for DS Penske, climbing from sixth to take the checkered flag for 25 points, while Maximilian Günther finished eleventh without scoring.

review.lastRace: A scoreless London E-Prix for Lola Yamaha ABT: Zane Maloney started eighteenth and finished seventeenth without points, while Lucas Di Grassi dropped from twentieth and did not finish.

Fifteenth on 13 points from 19 rounds, a point behind team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto and without any wins or podiums. He started 10th in the Mexico City Grand Prix but dropped to fourteenth for no points.

Sixteenth in the standings with 65 points across 18 rounds and no wins or podiums. He trails Fermin Aldeguer by a comfortable margin. In Malaysia he finished tenth for six points.
23rd in the championship with just 11 points from 18 rounds, no wins and no podiums. He is well off the pace of the front-runners. His Malaysian GP result was fifteenth for one point.
Sitting last of the Ducati riders with zero points after 18 rounds, no wins and no podiums so far in the campaign.

22nd with 14 points from 18 rounds and no wins or podiums. He finished 14th in Malaysia for two points, which puts him ahead of team-mates Pol Espargaro (5) and Jonas Folger (0), though all three sit at the rear.
25th with 5 points from 18 rounds and no wins or podiums. He trails team-mate Maverick Viñales, who sits 22nd on 14 points, leaving him near the back of the field.
29th and off the board with zero points from 18 rounds, no wins and no podiums. He is behind both team-mates Maverick Viñales (14) and Pol Espargaro (5), making him KTM's lowest scorer.
13th with 117 points from 18 rounds — the strongest of the Honda riders here — though still without a win or podium. His most recent race was a seventh-place finish in Malaysia worth 9 points.
15th with 78 points from 18 rounds and no wins or podiums, behind team-mate Luca Marini. In Malaysia he failed to finish, on zero points and without a classified position.

18th with 33 points from 18 rounds and no wins or podiums. He sits behind team-mates Luca Marini, Diogo Moreira and Johann Zarco, and did not finish in Malaysia for zero points.
26th with just 3 points from 18 rounds and no wins or podiums, trailing all of his Honda team-mates including Luca Marini (13th) and Joan Mir (18th).

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) won the Mexico City Grand Prix from grid five, holding off pole-starting Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) by 0.799 for a second place that also carried the fastest lap. Antonelli (Mercedes) was third, +4.006 back. The classification shows Verstappen's drive up from fifth to take a narrow win over Hamilton's front-row Ferrari. Points finished Lind ninth, Bortoleto eighth and Hirakawa tenth; five cars retired including both Aston Martin entries.
highlights: Max Verstappen started fifth and won the Mexico City Grand Prix for Red Bull, 0.799 ahead of Hamilton.
Lewis Hamilton took pole but finished second for Ferrari, also claiming the fastest lap of the race.
Liam Lawson started on grid twenty-two and finished seventh for RB F1 Team to score points.
Five cars retired: Arvid Lindblad, Oliver Bearman, Valtteri Bottas, Lance Stroll and Fernando Alonso all failed to finish.

review.summary: Marc Marquez won the Grand Prix of Malaysia for Ducati Lenovo Team, with Pedro Acosta second for Red Bull KTM Factory Racing and Alex Marquez third for BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP on the podium. Points were spread across a wide run of finishers, while Johann Zarco, Diogo Moreira, Joan Mir and Augusto Fernandez were left unclassified after not completing the race.
highlights: Marc Marquez won the Grand Prix of Malaysia for Ducati Lenovo Team to claim the full 25 points.
Pedro Acosta finished second for Red Bull KTM Factory Racing and Alex Marquez third for BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP on the podium.
Johann Zarco, Diogo Moreira, Joan Mir and Augusto Fernandez were all left unclassified after not completing the race.

review.summary: Taylor Barnard won for DS Penske from sixth on the grid, holding off Mahindra Racing's Nyck De Vries and Edoardo Mortara to complete a front-row podium. The classification shows a front-run Porsche that fell away: Pascal Wehrlein started third but finished fourteenth, with fourth-placed grid driver Nico Müller down to twelfth.
highlights: Oliver Rowland climbed eight places from seventeenth on the grid to finish ninth for Nissan.
Taylor Barnard won for DS Penske, climbing five places from sixth on the grid.
Pascal Wehrlein started third but finished fourteenth, with fourth-placed grid driver Nico Müller down to twelfth.
